title: Capturing the RNA-binding proteome from plants using organic phase separation
author: Sánchez-Camargo, Kramer, et al.

steps.title: Prepare buffer stocks
steps.instruction: Prepare all buffers listed below exactly as described, using high‑purity reagents and DEPC treatment where indicated. Store each buffer under the specified conditions.

substeps.instruction: Lysis buffer (base) – 1 L: dissolve 100 mM MOPS, 2 % CTAB, 20 mM EDTA, 1.4 M NaCl in deionized water, adjust pH to 7.0, filter through a 0.22 µm bottle‑top vacuum filter into a sterile autoclaved bottle with a magnetic stir bar; optionally aliquot 250 mL, add DEPC to 0.2 % and stir overnight, remove stir bar, autoclave at 121 °C for ≥17 min, protect from light, store 20–25 °C up to 6 months.
DEPC‑treated water – 2 L: fill four 500 mL bottles with ddH₂O, add DEPC to 0.1 % (v/v), mix, incubate ≥2 h at room temperature, autoclave, store indefinitely at 20–25 °C.
1 M Tris pH 8.0 – 500 mL: dissolve Tris in DEPC‑treated ddH₂O to 1 M, adjust pH to 8.0 with HCl, autoclave, store indefinitely at 20–25 °C.
0.5 M EDTA pH 8.0 – 250 mL: dissolve EDTA in DEPC‑treated ddH₂O to 0.5 M, adjust pH to 8.0 with NaOH pellets, autoclave, store indefinitely at 20–25 °C.
5 M NaCl – 250 mL: dissolve NaCl to 5 M, treat with 0.2 % DEPC, autoclave, store indefinitely at 20–25 °C.
50× Complete protease inhibitor – prepare by dissolving one tablet in 1 mL 10 mM Tris pH 8.0; store up to 12 weeks at –20 °C.
TE‑SDS 0.5% – 100 mL: combine 10 mM Tris pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 0.5 % SDS, treat with 0.2 % DEPC, incubate overnight at 37 °C to inactivate DEPC, store indefinitely at 20–25 °C.
3 M sodium acetate pH 5.2 – 100 mL: dissolve sodium acetate to 3 M, adjust pH to 5.2 with glacial acetic acid, treat with 0.2 % DEPC, autoclave, store indefinitely at 20–25 °C.
0.2 M sodium citrate pH 6.0 – 50 mL: dissolve sodium citrate to 0.2 M, adjust pH to 6.0 with HCl, treat with 0.2 % DEPC, autoclave, protect from light, store at 4 °C.
70 % and 80 % ethanol – prepare by diluting molecular‑biology‑grade ethanol with sterile DEPC‑treated water to the desired concentration; store up to 1 month in airtight containers at 20–25 °C.
2× RNA fragmentation buffer – 50 mL: mix 20 mM Tris pH 8.0 and 50 mM MgCl₂, treat with 0.2 % DEPC, autoclave, store up to 1 month at 4 °C.
100 mM PMSF – dissolve PMSF in isopropanol to 100 mM, aliquot 0.5 mL, store at –20 °C for up to 6 months.
50 mM TEAB – prepare fresh from 1 M stock in UltraPure water immediately before use.

2× Proteinase K reaction buffer – 50 mL: combine 50 mM Tris pH 8.0, 40 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 4 % SDS, 250 mM NaCl; treat with 0.2 % DEPC, mix well, incubate overnight at 37 °C to inactivate DEPC, store up to 1 month at 20–25 °C protected from light.

steps.title: Elute and purify RNA‑bound proteins
steps.instruction: Release RNA‑bound proteins by RNA degradation, then precipitate the proteins for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge methanol‑precipitated samples (from previous step) at maximum speed for 30 min at 4 °C; during centrifugation prepare 2× RNA fragmentation buffer.
Decant supernatant carefully.
Wash pellet once with 70 % ethanol, remove residual ethanol, and air‑dry as described earlier.
Resuspend pellet in 300 µL UltraPure water, vortex gently, then incubate at 4 °C for 15–30 min with occasional vortexing (pre‑heat a heat block to 95 °C for later step).
Divide the resuspended interphase into two 150 µL aliquots: keep one as backup at –20 °C (for RNA analysis) and use the other for protein release.
Add 150 µL 2× RNA fragmentation buffer to the working aliquot and mix thoroughly.
Incubate at 95 °C for 7 min in a heat block, then cool to room temperature for 2 min.
Add 10 µL RNase A/T1 mix, vortex, and incubate at 37 °C for 3 h (do not increase enzyme concentration).
Stop the reaction by adding 300 µL Trizol LS and 100 µL chloroform, vortex, and incubate 3 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 min to separate phases.

Tilt the tube and use a 200 µL pipette to collect 190 µL from the bottom of the organic phase (protein‑containing layer) without disturbing the interphase; transfer to a polypropylene Protein LoBind 2 mL tube.
Add 1.8 mL methanol to the collected organic phase and incubate overnight at –20 °C (pause point; samples can be stored up to 1 week).

steps.title: Analyze proteomics data
steps.instruction: Process mass‑spectrometry output with MaxQuant and Perseus to identify RBPs enriched in cross‑linked fractions and generate volcano plots.

substeps.instruction: After peptide‑spectrum matching, obtain the proteinGroups.txt file.
Download the supplementary data package (Data S1 – starprotocol_demo.zip) and extract it to the working directory.
Copy the annotation file annot_nbenth_MPP_v7.txt to Desktop/Perseus/bin/conf/annotations.
Load annot_nbenth_MPP_v7.txt in Perseus (Matrix → Generic matrix upload → select proteinGroups.txt, choose the 18 LFQ intensity columns, move to “Main”, press OK).
Filter out rows labelled Potential contaminants, Reverse hits, and Proteins identified only by site (Filter rows → Filter rows based on categorical column).
Annotate biological replicates by loading grouping_fraction.txt (Annot. rows → Categorical annotation rows → Read from file).
Filter for reproducibility: keep proteins present in ≥70 % of values in at least one group (Filter rows → Filter rows based on valid values → Percentage = 70, In at least one group).
Add additional annotations from annot_nbenth_MPP_v7.txt (Annot. columns → Add annotation → select file, import all metadata).
Log2‑transform LFQ intensities (Basic → Transform).
Impute missing values from a normal distribution using default settings (Imputation → Replace missing values from normal distribution).
Perform a two‑sample Welch’s t‑test: Tests → Two‑sample test, set group 1 = OOPS_XL, group 2 = OOPS_NOXL, select Welch’s t‑test.
Export the test results as starprotocol_rbpome.txt (Export → Generic matrix export).
Open starprotocol_rbpome.txt in a spreadsheet, delete the second row (Perseus metadata).
Filter column “Welch’s T-test Significant OOPS_XL_OOPS_NOXL” to retain only “+” entries (reduces to 431 protein groups).
Further filter column “Welch’s T-test Difference OOPS_XL_OOPS_NOXL” to keep entries with fold change ≥1 (leaves 369 enriched RBPs).
Save the filtered list as starprotocol_enriched_RBPome.txt.

Generate volcano plots in RStudio: place both starprotocol_rbpome.txt and starprotocol_enriched_RBPome.txt in the same folder, edit volcano_rbpome.R to set the working directory, run the script to produce volcano_rbps_starprotocol.pdf.
Optional: generate volcano plots directly in Perseus using the matrix from step 75 (select OOPS_XL vs OOPS_NOXL).
Use the final list of enriched RBPs for downstream analyses, validation, or hypothesis generation.

steps.title: Purify RNA with DNase and proteinase K
steps.instruction: Isolate high‑quality RNA from the RNA‑containing interphase, remove DNA and residual proteins, and precipitate the RNA.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the RNA‑containing samples (collected in step 19) at maximum speed for 15 min at 4 °C to pellet RNA.
Wash the RNA pellet with 1 mL 70 % ethanol, vortex thoroughly.
Centrifuge 5 min at maximum speed, remove residual ethanol, and air‑dry the pellet as described earlier.
Resuspend pellet in 500 µL 1 mM sodium citrate pH 6.0.
Quantify RNA using a NanoDrop (expect A260/A280 < 2.0, A260/A230 ≈ 2.2).
Transfer 30–50 µg RNA to a new 2 mL tube (store remaining sample at –80 °C).
Adjust volume to 85 µL with UltraPure water.
Prepare DNase I master mix: per sample add 5 µL DNase I and 10 µL 10× DNase buffer; mix gently.
Add 15 µL DNase I master mix to each RNA sample, mix gently, and incubate at 37 °C for 45 min.
During DNase incubation, prepare 2× proteinase K reaction buffer.
Stop DNase reaction by adding 110 µL 2× proteinase K reaction buffer, then add 10 µL proteinase K and mix thoroughly.
Incubate at 55 °C for 1.5 h (shaking at 550 rpm if available) to degrade DNase and cross‑linked proteins.
Add 660 µL TE‑SDS 0.5%, 120 µL 5 M NaCl, and 2 µL glycogen; vortex thoroughly.
Add 1 mL isopropanol, mix, and incubate ≥2 h or overnight at –20 °C to precipitate RNA.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 30 min at 4 °C, remove supernatant.
Wash pellet twice with 70 % ethanol and air‑dry as before.
Resuspend RNA in 50 µL 1 mM sodium citrate pH 6.0.
Quantify the purified RNA by the preferred method.

steps.title: Perform RT‑qPCR
steps.instruction: Reverse‑transcribe RNA into cDNA and quantify transcript levels by quantitative PCR.

substeps.instruction: Prepare RNA‑primer mix (10 µL total): 0.5–2.5 µg RNA, 1 µL random hexamers (50 µM), 1 µL oligo‑dT (50 µM), add water to 10 µL. For non‑crosslinked controls use the same volume as the corresponding crosslinked fraction.
Denature RNA‑primer mix at 70 °C for 5 min, then place on ice.
Prepare RT master mix per sample (9 µL): 1.5 µL water, 4 µL 5× RT buffer, 2 µL dNTPs (0.2 mM each), 0.5 µL RNase inhibitor, 1 µL reverse transcriptase.
Add 9 µL RT master mix to each RNA‑primer tube, mix, briefly spin.
Run RT program: 25 °C 10 min (primer annealing), 42 °C 60 min (reverse transcription), 85 °C 5 min (enzyme inactivation).
Adjust cDNA concentration to 25 ng/µL (based on input RNA) using 10 mM Tris pH 8.0; store cDNA at –20 °C or –80 °C.
Prepare qPCR master mix per reaction (14 µL): 9 µL water, 3 µL 5× HOT FIREPol EvaGreen qPCR Supermix, 1 µL primer 1 (3 µM), 1 µL primer 2 (3 µM).

Add 1 µL cDNA to each qPCR tube/well, spin 1 min at 1000 × g, and run qPCR with the following program: 95 °C 12 min (initial activation), then 40 cycles of 95 °C 15 s (denaturation) followed by 60 °C 60 s (annealing/extension, fluorescence detection); finish with a melt‑curve.
Generate a standard curve to assess primer efficiency and check for inhibitors.
Calculate relative transcript abundance using the ΔCt method, normalizing Ct values to the non‑crosslinked aqueous phase (set as 1). Use the formula %RNA = 100 · 2^(–(Ctfraction – CtNon – CLaq)).

description: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate RNA-related processes such as RNA splicing, nuclear export, stability, relocalization to e.g., processing (P-)bodies, and translation, as well as post-transcriptional gene silencing.1 They function by recognizing specific RNA motifs or structures through canonical RNA recognition domains and also through low-complexity regions such as intrinsically disordered domains.2,3,4 Despite their essential roles in development, environmental adaptation, and stress responses, the functional diversity and molecular mechanisms of plant RBPs remain poorly characterized.5,6,7,8 Orthogonal Organic Phase Separation (OOPS) is a method that allows the global identification of RBPs without relying on specific protein tags or polyadenylated RNA, which is the case for RNA interactome capture.9,10,11 It uses UV light to crosslink RNA-protein complexes in vivo, followed by repeated phenol-chloroform extractions, during which RNA-protein adducts accumulate at the interphase. This separation enables the analysis of both proteins and RNA present at the interphase (Figure 1). This type of approach and other variants have been successfully used in animal and bacterial systems,10,14 and more recently in plants, where over 2,000 RBPs have been identified from Arabidopsis tissues.11,15,16,17Figure 1Overview of the OOPS protocolPlant leaves are harvested and crosslinked using UV light at 254 nm. The tissue is then frozen and ground, and lysis is performed using a custom CTAB buffer, followed by clarification of the lysate. Phase separation with phenol-chloroform produces two main phases (aqueous and organic) and an interphase containing the crosslinked RNA-protein fraction. Successive rounds of organic re-extraction remove contaminants from the interphase. High-quality protein and RNA are produced for downstream analysis. RNA and protein drawings were retrieved from NIAID NIH BioArt Source.12,13
